story.headline: Australia is one of ten governments to sign the US-led San Francisco Declaration to protect AI supply chains, as Albanese meets Trump at the Quad in Manila tonight

linkedin.post:
Ten governments, Australia among them, have signed the San Francisco Declaration: a US-led pact to protect the chips, minerals, power and data centres behind AI.

Canberra says it is about securing the supply chains Australia relies on. Olivia Shen of the United States Studies Centre says it binds Australia more closely to the US. Indonesia and Malaysia have joined China's rival AI body, and the IEA says China does more than 90% of rare earth refining.

Does Washington's AI pact make Australia more secure, or more exposed to Beijing? Tell us what you think below.

#AusSight #geopolitics #AI

warnings: The IEA's 'above 90%' figure is China's share of rare earth refining specifically; ABC's wider claim (over 90% for several minerals incl. graphite and gallium) was not used.
Olivia Shen's view ('continues to bind us more closely to the US') and the Albanese office's 'supply chains we rely on are secure' line are single-source (ABC News, 17 Nov 2026).
ABC lists Vietnam among ASEAN backers of China's rival AI body; The Star's founding-member list (16 Jul 2026) does not, so the video and posts name only Indonesia and Malaysia.
No real person is shown on screen: Wikimedia Commons was rate-limited (HTTP 429) all run, so the Albanese portrait could not be downloaded, and ParlView was unreachable.
Video is 56.1s, slightly above the 40-55s target (within the 60s maximum).
